# Paravitāraṇakathā (Kv 2.4)

**ID:** Kv 2.4
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Paravitāraṇakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paravitāraṇakathā* (Kv 2.4) is the fourth debate of the second chapter (*vagga*) of the Abhidhamma treatise *Kathāvatthu*. It examines the thesis *atthi arahato paravitāraṇā* ("an arahant can be guided or instructed by others"), which corresponds to the fourth proposition of the celebrated "Five Points" attributed in early sectarian traditions to Mahādeva [Williams 2000; Skorupski 1991; Dutt 1978]. In this debate, opposing schools maintained that an arahant might acquire knowledge or develop faith through the instruction and guidance of a preceptor rather than entirely on their own, drawing distinctions between types of arahants [Dutt 1978; Dube 1980]. The Theravādin interlocutor rejects this contention, arguing that an arahant has completely overcome delusion (*vītamoha*), possesses the Dhamma-eye (*dhammacakkhu*), and realizes liberation directly without being dependent on others (*na paravitāraṇā*) [Dutt 1978; Dube 1980]. Buddhaghosa glosses the term by explaining that opponents consider that others elucidate, reveal, or declare those matters to them (*pare vitaranti pakāsenti ācikkhanti*) [Dutt 1945]. Modern scholars have discussed the translation of *paravitāraṇā*, noting early renderings such as "excelled by others" alongside interpretations of "induced investigation," "comprehension by others," or "bringing across," which align closely with Tibetan (*yongs su brtag pa*) and Chinese (*ta ling ru*) counterparts found in non-Theravāda records [Eckel 2008; Skorupski 1991; Williams 2000; Yao 2005].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Mentioned in: Snp 5.6 (PTS Snp 204) Dhotakamāṇavapucchā; Cnd 2 Pucchā; Cnd 9 Dhotakamāṇavapucchāniddesa; Mnd 2 Guhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa

**Sources**

- [Dutt 1978] Nalinaksha Dutt, Buddhist Sects in India (1978) — Details on the doctrinal thesis, the Theravāda stance (vītamoha, na paravitāraṇā), and sectarian interlocutors.
- [Dutt 1945] Nalinaksha Dutt, Early Monastic Buddhism, vol. 2 (1945) — Doctrinal debate summary and quotation from Buddhaghosa's commentary.
- [Dube 1980] S. N. Dube, Cross Currents in Early Buddhism (1980) — Arguments regarding the dhammacakkhu and preceptor guidance across types of arahants.
- [Skorupski 1991] L. S. Cousins, in T. Skorupski (ed.), The Buddhist Forum, vol. 2 (1991) — Analysis of the four possible meanings of paravitāraṇā within the Five Points tradition.
- [Williams 2000] Paul Williams (ed.), Buddhism: Critical Concepts in Religious Studies, vol. 2 (2000) — Context within the Five Points verse and discussion of translation terminology.
- [Eckel 2008] Malcolm David Eckel, Bhāviveka and His Buddhist Opponents (2008) — Discussion of the Tibetan rendering yongs su brtag pa and its relation to Pali paravitāraṇā.
- [Yao 2005] Zhihua Yao, The Buddhist Theory of Self-Cognition (2005) — Tibetan and Chinese terminology corresponding to the fourth point paravitāraṇa.
